'''Zygerria''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the distant corners of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Species/Legends|species]], whose members lived in walled [[Fortress/Legends|fortresses]] high atop mesas. Zygerria was famous throughout the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] for its notorious [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] markets and served as the headquarters of the [[Zygerrian Slavers Guild]]. A major supporter of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Zygerrian Slavers Guild later provided the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Empire]] with disposable laborers for a number of construction projects.

==Description==
Zygerria was a terrestrial<ref name="CW3" /><ref name="SR" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="SWE:Z" /> located in the [[Zygerria system/Legends|eponymous star system]]<ref name="CW3" /><ref name="EAOC" /> of the near-lawless<ref name="WZT" /> [[Chorlian sector/Legends|Chorlian sector]],<ref name="CEZ" /><ref name="EAOC" /><ref name="FD" /> in the [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Trans-Hydian]] portion of<ref name="Region" /> the distant corners of<ref name="GW" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]],<ref name="CEZ" /><ref name="EA" /><ref name="FD" /> almost in [[Wild Space/Legends|Wild Space]].<ref name="WZT" /> Zygerria lay on two small [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]]: the [[Shaltin Tunnels/Legends|Shaltin Tunnels]], which connected it with the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]] and the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]], and the [[Listehol Run/Legends|Listehol Run]], through which Zygerria had access to the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]].<ref name="EA" />

[[File:FlyingBrezak.jpg|left|thumb|250px|A pair of [[brezak/Legends|brezak]] creatures flying above the airy plains of Zygerria]]
Zygerria was a chilly,<ref name="WZT" /><ref name="CEZ" /> picturesque [[Planet/Legends|world]] with [[Fortress/Legends|fortress]]-capped mesas that extended above windswept plains. Graceful [[Brezak/Legends|brezak]] creatures caught the wind currents and soared effortlessly from butte to butte. The deceiving beauty of the planet hid the fact that Zygerria's [[City/Legends|cities]] were all built upon the backs of [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]].<ref name="SWE:Z" />

==History==
===Early history===
{{Quote|Slavery is the natural order of things. The weak deserve nothing more than to kneel before the strong, bound to our service.|Queen [[Miraj Scintel/Legends|Miraj Scintel]]|<ref name="SR" />}}
At least as early as [[30,000 BBY]], Zygerria was under the control of the [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]], an ancient [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning [[Politics/Legends|empire]] ruled by the advanced [[Species/Legends|species]] [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]], who hailed from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. The Rakata used their knowledge to conquer and [[Slavery/Legends|enslave]] other species throughout the galaxy until the empire's [[Rakatan Civil War|collapse]] in [[25,200 BBY]].<ref name="EA" />

Ultimately, a civilization of a violent [[Species/Legends|species]] known as the [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrians]] emerged on Zygerria. Their society was built on the principle that strength led to authority, and for Zygerrians, strength could take many forms – not only physical strength, but also strength of will, conviction, and bravery. Raised in a culture where weakness could mean [[Death/Legends|death]] or enslavement, Zygerrians cultivated a dangerous and unpredictable image to deter others from challenging their dominance.<ref name="GW" />

The Zygerrian people were organized into clans<ref name="WZT" /> and classes. They had a [[Noble/Legends|noble]] class, many members of which, despite their high status, pursued a career in the military.<ref name="GW" /> The Zygerrian [[Head of State/Legends|Head of State]] was a [[Monarchy/Legends|monarch]]; female rulers held the title of [[Queen/Legends|queen]],<ref name="SR" /> fully styled as [[Queen of Zygerria/Legends|The Most High Queen of Zygerria]],<ref name="CW3" /> while males were addressed as [[King/Legends|kings]].<ref name="FLT" />

===Lost glory===
{{Quote|Thrived on Outer Rim slave trade for centuries did the Zygerrian civilization. Moved from system to system, abducting primitive beings to enslave for profit – even into the systems of the Republic. When ordered to cease, resist did the Zygerrians. Crushed their Empire of Bondage did the Jedi. Ruined were these slavers, but refuse they did to change their ways. Into obscurity they fell...|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]]|<ref name="CW2">[[The Clone Wars 2|''The Clone Wars'' 2]]</ref>}}
[[Millennium/Legends|Millennia]] before the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was [[Declaration of a New Order|proclaimed]] the [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrians]] subjugated entire [[Planet/Legends|planets]] and civilizations throughout the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Their [[Zygerrian Slave Empire/Legends|slaving empire]] stretched from [[Argazda/Legends|Argazda]] down the [[Salin Corridor/Legends|Salin Corridor]] and encompassed the entire [[Triellus Trade Route/Legends|Triellus Trade Route]] to [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] along the [[Corellian Run/Legends|Corellian Run]]. The Zygerrian Empire supplied [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]] to several Outer Rim powers, including the [[Chevin/Legends|Chevins]] of [[Vinsoth/Legends|Vinsoth]] and the sprawling [[Hutt Empire]].<ref name="FLT" /> For several thousand years<ref name="SWE:Z" /><ref name="FLT" /> Zygerria prospered transporting sentient beings as product, labor to be bought, sold and traded in markets scattered across the galaxy.<ref name="SWEZN" /> The Zygerrian Slave Empire grew wealthy and powerful, as did those who exploited their chained subjects.<ref name="SR" /><ref name="SWE:Z" />

The space surrounding Zygerria was explored by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic]] [[Scout/Legends|explorations]] between [[3000 BBY|3000]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. During the final four years of the [[Light and Darkness War]], Zygerria was situated within the space controlled by the [[New Sith]].<ref name="EA" />

[[File:Jedi_Zygerrian_conflict.jpg|right|thumb|280px|The Jedi Knights targeted the Zygerrian Slave Empire in an effort to abolish its slave trade]]
When slavery was outlawed in [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] space,<ref name="SWEZN" /> the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] spearheaded a [[Outer Rim anti-slavery campaign|campaign]] to abolish slavery in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], which primarily targeted the Zygerrians. After a [[Jedi–Zygerrian conflict/Legends|brutal conflict]], the Zygerrian Empire fractured, and its power base crumbled. Having lost their power and influence, the Zygerrians retreated to their homeworld to pick up the pieces.<ref name="FLT" /> Zygerrian old [[Fortress/Legends|fortresses]] and slave markets remained impressive edifices, though their luster had faded with time. Some Zygerrians actively plotted a return to the old ways<ref name="SWE:Z" /> and spent millennia rebuilding their empire.<ref name="FLT" /> After the empire's collapse, these buildings remained impressive sights to tourists, bringing visitors even from [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]].<ref name="EFKTG">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep411|text="Kidnapped" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide"|nolive=1}}</ref>

===Chance for revival===
{{Quote|Zygerria will be rich and powerful again. The Jedi will not stop us this time.|[[Darts D'Nar/Legends|Darts D'Nar]]|<ref name="TCW11">{{TCW|Kidnapped}}</ref>}}
By the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="SR" /><ref name="FLT" /> the ruling [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Miraj Scintel/Legends|Miraj Scintel]] longed for a return to glory for her people and took advantage of a Republic distracted by war to expand the slave trade, allied by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist Alliance]].<ref name="SWEMS">{{SWE|characters|queenmirajscintel|Queen Miraj Scintel}}</ref> The Zygerrians had once again become a dominant force in [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] trafficking, rebranded as the [[Zygerrian Slavers Guild]]. With the blessing of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] and the aid of [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]], the Zygerrians preyed upon helpless [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] isolated by the war. They established outposts on far-off worlds such as [[Kowak/Legends|Kowak]] and [[Listehol/Legends|Listehol]] to support their efforts, creating satellite markets to expand their influence and restore their former glory.<ref name="FLT" /> In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="FF">{{FactFile2014|59|20 BBY 29-32|Slaves of Zygerria}}</ref> after the ruthless [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] of Zygerria<ref name="SWEAM">{{SWE|characters|ataimolec|Atai Molec}}</ref> [[Atai Molec/Legends|Atai Molec]] overthrew the Queen Scintel<ref name="SR" /><ref name="FLT" /> and assumed the throne, the Zygerrian Slave Empire was reborn.<ref name="FLT" />

[[File:AtaiMolecHS-SWE.png|thumb|left|200px|As king of Zygerria, Atai Molec declared the rebirth of the Zygerrian Slave Empire]]
Barring setbacks during the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Reconquest of the Rim|reconquest]] of the Rim,<ref name="FLT" /> when the Imperial [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] proceeded to [[Siege of Zygerria|besiege]] Zygerria and forced the Zygerrians to negotiate peace with an [[Unidentified Imperial Advisor|Imperial advisor]].<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Despite this, the Zygerrian Empire's expansion had gone largely unchecked since the formation of the Empire. The Zygerrian monarchy negotiated a deal with the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] to restrict slaving operations to the Outer Rim in exchange for amnesty from Imperial sovereignty. The Zygerrian Empire renewed its ties with the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidics]] and once again became the premier source of enslaved [[Togruta/Legends|Togrutas]], [[Theelin/Legends|Theelins]], and [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'leks]] in the Outer Rim.<ref name="FLT" /> In addition, the Zygerrian Slavers Guild provided the Empire with disposable laborers for its numerous construction projects.<ref name="FD" /> At this time, Zygerria, along with [[Karazak/Legends|Karazak]] and the [[Thalassian system]], was considered one of the Outer Rim's slavery capitals.<ref name="GG9" />

===Rise of the New Republic===
Following the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|fall]] of the Galactic Empire, Zygerria was one of many worlds [[Zsinj's Empire|controlled]] by Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|Warlord]] [[Zsinj]] prior to his [[Battle of Dathomir (Hunt for Zsinj)|death]] in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]].<ref name="EA" /> As the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] established itself as the galactic government, they passed laws that outlawed slavery. The Zygerrian slaving guilds lost a lot of their influence and power. However, despite this ban, slavery was still conducted in criminal havens, and remnants of the Zygerrian slavers' guilds continued to supply a steady stream of slaves to criminal organisations such as the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Kajidic/Legends|Kajidics]].<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

In [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], on the [[Caamas Document Crisis|eve]] of the end of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> the Chorlian sector, where the Zygerria star system was located,<ref name="EAOC" /> was represented in the [[New Republic Senate/Legends|New Republic Senate]].<ref name="SP">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Introduction===
Zygerria as «Zygeria» was first mentioned in ''[[Galaxy Guide 9: Fragments from the Rim]]'', a [[1993]] sourcebook written by [[Simon Smith]] and [[Eric S. Trautmann]] for [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="GG9" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the [[Zygerria system/Legends|Zygerria star system]], and therefore Zygerria, in grid square S-4.<ref name="EA" />

====''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' continuity====
[[File:Zygerria-TheCloneWars2.jpg|thumb|right|150px|The Zygerrian Royal Palace as depicted in the ''Slaves of the Republic'' comic books]]
The Zygerrian species played a substantial role in the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (multimedia project)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' multimedia project]]. Writer [[Henry Gilroy]] originally developed a story outline involving the Zygerrians while working on the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'' television series]]. However, Gilroy's proposed story was deemed too complex for the series at that point, so it was not produced as episodes for the show.<ref name="CS4">{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|featurette=The Slaves of Zygerria}}</ref> Instead, Gilroy's story was realized as [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Slaves of the Republic|''Slaves of the Republic'']], a [[2008]] story arc of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (comic series)|''The Clone Wars'' comic series]]. Written by Gilroy himself and illustrated by [[Scott Hepburn]], this story tied into the television series.<ref name="CW2" />

[[George Lucas]], the creator of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' franchise, liked Gilroy's comic story enough to request that it be adapted as future episodes of the show. In [[2011]]–[[2012]], the ''Slaves of the Republic'' comics were adapted into three episodes of the television series, titled "[[Kidnapped]]," "[[Slaves of the Republic]]," and "[[Escape from Kadavo]]." The episodes followed the same premise as the comics but featured several plot differences.<ref name="CS4" />
